verdict: RUNG (the subclass with its domain switched off reproduces share_instruct): worst error 0.00e+00 across 5 cells (tolerance 1e-09). Bit-identical, so the templated arm differs from the raw one in the DOMAIN and in nothing else. SIGNAL in the templated arm: T=0.02: spread 0.053 vs seed noise 0.008 OK; T=0.7: spread 0.016 vs seed noise 0.007 OK. 2 of 2 constructions carry model signal above seed noise. PRIMARY, agreement between the RAW and TEMPLATED model rankings: T=0.02: rho=+0.400, T=0.7: rho=+0.300. Below 0.6 on 2 of 2 temperatures: the domain reorders the models, so F130's model-attributability is a RAW-DOMAIN statement and the reframed thesis needs revising again. SECONDARY, mean |shift| in top1 between domains: T=0.02: 0.1696, T=0.7: 0.0674. F135 already established the VALUES do not transfer; this is reported for comparability, not as news. BOUNDARY: 5 instruction-tuned models, one template each, N=96, B=16, settle=16, r=2, and only 2 of share_instruct's four temperatures ([0.02, 0.7]) -- the templated cell costs 1617s against the raw run's 150s, so the full grid was ~18 hours and the extremes were kept. Base models have no template and cannot be run on this axis. One template is one domain, so this shows whether the ranking survives THIS domain change, not domain changes in general.

_analysis_provenance.note: sha256 of the analysis source at write time, plus the repo-local import closure. If any of these does not match the file on disk, the analysis was produced by a different version of the code -- re-run it before reading the numbers (issue #38; the imports half closes the same hole one level down the import graph). Third-party package versions are NOT covered.
